title: Switch to a new broadband package
intent: An existing customer moves to a different package on the same line.
variationBecause: Ask for the postcode first, so we only show packages the customer can actually get.

screens.purpose: The customer tells us where the line is, before seeing anything they might not be able to have.

props.heading: Where is your line?
props.explain: We will only show you packages we can actually deliver to this address.

annotations: This is the whole point of the variation: nothing is offered that cannot be delivered, so no choice is taken away later.
Cost of the reversal — the customer is asked to do work before being shown any reason to care.

screens.purpose: The customer picks from the packages their line can actually carry.

props.message: Full Fibre is available at 12 Example Street.

props.heading: Choose a new package
props.explain: These are the packages we can deliver to your address.

annotations: Essential is absent because it is not available here — the customer never learns it exists. Whether that is a kindness or a lost sale is exactly the business conversation.
The status block is new in this variation. It carries the answer to the question the customer just did work to ask.

screens.purpose: The customer adds optional services before committing.

props.heading: Anything else?
props.explain: You can add or remove these later without changing your contract.

screens.purpose: The customer confirms who they are and how to reach them.

props.heading: Your details
props.explain: We already have your address. We just need a way to reach you.

annotations: Shorter than the base journey's version of this screen, because the address is already known.

screens.purpose: The customer reviews everything and commits.

props.heading: Check and confirm
props.explain: Your new package starts on the next billing date.

annotations: Address is the first row here and the last row in the base journey. The summary follows the order the customer supplied things in.
